selected_by: operator request: reload AWA and prepare v0.0.1 for execution, 2026-10-22

stories.title: Keep the core Memory Bank usable offline
stories.outcome: A fresh agent can use the shared Markdown bank and portable skill without optional infrastructure.
acceptance: Initialize, inspect, edit, checkpoint and resume using files and the skill with all optional services disabled.
No hosted service, model, client, daemon, embedding, MCP or hook is a core prerequisite.
Same-repository Git publication and turn-boundary memory refresh are part of v0.0.1; local use remains available offline while sharing is pending.
Keep AWA work/delivery evidence, Vox coordination, and durable memory under their separate authorities.
stories.validation: Run an isolated file-and-skill resume walkthrough with generated state removed.

stories.title: Define explicit memory scopes and retrieval consent
stories.outcome: The shared model and skill make project scope the default and cross-scope access explicit.
acceptance: Shared repository knowledge is the memory unit; component, branch, task and session conditions refine applicability.
Cross-project retrieval is explicit; personal profiles, private per-developer banks and personal preference stores are excluded.
Developer identity supports provenance and clarification, never a personal namespace or separate memory ACL.
stories.validation: Review the scope matrix against isolation fixtures and portable instructions.

stories.title: Resolve memory conflicts using stronger authorities
stories.outcome: Memory points to current authorities and routes conflicts to correction.
acceptance: Preserve every authority in the ADR table, including work tracking, coordination and reviewed procedures.
A stronger current source wins over remembered text; memory never proves delivery or agent ownership.
A conflict can be recorded as a correction or revocation candidate.
stories.validation: Exercise conflicting code, ADR, user-preference and stale-memory fixtures.

stories.title: Keep current Markdown complete without application state
stories.outcome: The smallest useful Cline-shaped bank remains the canonical readable project state.
acceptance: Provide the six recognizable contexts and bounded MEMORY.md router while omitting irrelevant empty files.
Tracked banks link to Git/evidence; untracked or unpublished project learning reports local/pending sharing honestly.
Removing caches, journals and indexes leaves current memory complete and readable.
stories.validation: Initialize minimal tracked/untracked fixtures and resume after deleting generated state.

stories.title: Define one versioned lifecycle and current-selection predicate
stories.outcome: One machine-readable model defines lifecycle transitions and current visibility.
acceptance: Include candidate, quarantined, active, superseded, revoked, expired and deleted states.
Model correction/new version, replacement-aware supersession, revocation, expiry, new-evidence reactivation and terminal deletion.
Keep confidence, trust, visibility and valid time independent.
CLI, validators, tests and generated model guide share authorized-scope/active/time/trust/no-superseder selection semantics.
stories.validation: Validate the transition table and generated model/predicate agreement with state fixtures.

stories.title: Document the OS security boundary and authority precedence
stories.outcome: The product accurately explains raw-file access and the limits of local identities.
acceptance: Direct file access is governed by OS/repository/hosting access and cannot promise CLI audit or mediation.
Developer IDs provide provenance; they are neither authentication nor per-developer memory ACLs.
Developers with repository access use the same bank; tests and documentation preserve these limits.
stories.validation: Review security claims and run malicious-memory/manual-access canaries.

stories.title: Prove local banks stay independent of federation
stories.outcome: A single project can initialize, checkpoint, resume, search, validate and repair without any global service.
acceptance: Local Markdown stays readable, editable, versionable, exportable and useful.
No federation service/catalog is required for the baseline.
stories.validation: Run file-based workflow with all federation/optional state absent.

stories.title: Provide one offline public-interface contract-test gate
stories.outcome: One test command verifies the product contracts in completely isolated test worlds.
acceptance: Route pack/lifecycle/bank/concurrency/client/optional/evaluation layers through one gate, enabling later layers as their operations ship.
Acceptance uses real CLI/scripts/file workflows rather than internal helpers alone.
Isolate home/XDG/client/repo/bank/state/cache/backup roots; require no real credentials/network/live data.
stories.validation: Run the top-level gate from an empty temporary environment and verify live paths remain untouched.

stories.title: Create the minimal useful bank and bounded schema-bearing router
stories.outcome: A project bank has a precise, human-editable file contract.
acceptance: Default to repository-root memory-bank tracked as shared project memory.
Require MEMORY.md with byte-zero schema/project-id/router-updated frontmatter.
Routes carry relative Markdown path, purpose, scope, lifecycle and read conditions; router time is not every-file revision.
Create useful recognizable context files only and link volatile/authoritative claims to stronger sources.
Exclude disposable pending/runtime/recovery state from shared routes and do not maintain a second durable bank or personal overlay.
stories.validation: Validate minimal and expanded bank fixtures, omission routes and fresh-agent resume.

stories.title: Serialize mediated writers and reject unobserved external edits
stories.outcome: A bank-wide exclusive lock and base hashes protect mediated mutations.
acceptance: Exclusive-create lock precedes inventory and remains through readback/receipt; record random operation ID, host, PID, operation and start.
Second writer stops; stale recovery proves same-host process death or uses explicit operator review for another host.
Compute/recheck target hashes immediately before replacement; stop on external edits.
Document filesystem capability and non-cooperating manual-writer limits.
Locks govern one worktree only; exclude locks, transaction markers and recovery state from shared Git memory commits.
The safe mediated write baseline required by automatic capture and maintenance ships in v0.0.1.
stories.validation: Race actual writers and manual edits; test local/remote stale-lock refusal and recovery.

stories.title: Teach constrained manual checkpoint and external-change validation
stories.outcome: A client can safely follow the documented single-file manual fallback.
acceptance: Reread the target, change only the intended section and read back.
Treat a visible lock as do-not-edit and route interrupted banks to recovery.
Describe ordinary Markdown/Git recoverability without claiming audited mediated guarantees.
Subsequent mediated operations validate the external change instead of overwriting it.
stories.validation: Run a file-only checkpoint/resume walkthrough and a mediated external-change fixture when that surface ships.

stories.title: Define content-free durable tombstones for deleted memory
stories.outcome: Deleted sections or files cannot be recreated by projections and retain no sensitive fingerprint.
acceptance: Retain only random record ID, scope, deletion time, deletion authority and non-sensitive reason class.
Exclude content/evidence/secrets/personal data and reversible or low-entropy hashes.
Place safe tombstones in the project history whenever another projection could recreate deleted guidance.
stories.validation: Inspect tombstone fields and run delete/rebuild/resurrection canaries.

stories.title: Record stable developer attribution without personal memory namespaces
stories.outcome: Shared project learning identifies its originating developer across machines and harnesses.
acceptance: Aliases/evidence never silently replace the stable developer provenance ID.
Select another developer identity explicitly; no personal memory or preference data is stored in the attribution registry.
Repository and OS access govern the bank; developer IDs are not authentication or memory ACLs.
Explicitly adopt the same stable identity across two to five machines and keep collaborators distinct from harness/session identities.
Changing Git/hosting credentials never silently changes attribution; unknown/conflicting evidence remains visible.
stories.validation: Run install/developer selection fixtures with changed Git/client/user aliases.

stories.title: Resolve projects consistently across worktrees, remotes, moves and forks
stories.outcome: Stable bank IDs and repository evidence prevent accidental namespace splits or merges.
acceptance: Generate stable project IDs and bind observed locations/evidence; common Git directory joins linked worktrees.
Normalize credential/query/fragment/trailing-slash/.git and HTTPS/SSH/SCP syntax with host-specific case rules.
Preserve different hosts/owners/repos/forks; configured authority wins, otherwise use origin only if unambiguous.
Stop on conflicts/remote changes; no-remote moves keep identity; independent copies explicitly link or fork and rebinding retains alias history.
stories.validation: Run table-driven real repository/worktree/move/clone/fork/multiple-remote fixtures.

stories.title: Specify typed records with provenance and temporal validity
stories.outcome: Standalone records and optional history expose type, scope, provenance and changing truth.
acceptance: Support semantic fact, feedback, decision, attempt, result, reference and procedural candidate records.
Validate stable ID/schema, scope, kind/state, actor/source/evidence, time and derivation/correction links.
Record confidence, admission/trust/redaction metadata when required; mark visible stale statements explicitly.
Optional event history never contains the only readable current memory or replaces recovery journals.
Preserve originating developer identity, harness/session, evidence, and component/branch/revision/version/environment/prerequisite conditions.
Shared observations from unmerged work remain conditional; landing memory does not assert that main or an older branch has matching code.
stories.validation: Validate representative records and journal-loss fixtures against the schema.

stories.title: Expose bounded routes and consented session context
stories.outcome: Resume loads a bounded router and only the context relevant to the current task.
acceptance: MEMORY.md names purpose, validity and retrieval keys; detailed records load on demand.
Load the shared project router and relevant task/component context; maintain no personal profile or private memory layer.
Filter project scope, validity, trust and type before ranking; exact lookup works without embeddings.
Use turn-boundary memory-only refresh and applicability checks from ADR-0012.
stories.validation: Run representative file-only resume tasks and verify the selected file set.

stories.title: Build one progressive portable skill and shared model guide
stories.outcome: One registerable skill routes through shared domains to implemented operation leaves.
acceptance: Use discovery, root, domain and leaf layers; nested instructions use GUIDE.md.
Follow the linked blueprint loading order, leaf contract, conditional model reference and context-budget guardrails.
Add routes only for implemented operations; leaves require their domain and do not depend on unstated sibling rules.
Use uppercase RFC 2119 requirements and keep client policy outside core semantics.
Include implemented refresh and publication routes plus automatic capture/deduplication/consolidation/pruning under the shared domain/leaf rules.
Initialization follows ADR-0010 evidence discovery and focused clarification; refresh preserves code and local unpublished memory.
stories.validation: Validate the pack and perform representative initialize/resume/manual-checkpoint walkthroughs from only loaded instructions.

stories.title: Ship structural, lifecycle, isolation, deletion and poisoning canaries
stories.outcome: The first published release has executable canaries for every required baseline risk.
acceptance: Cover structural routes, lifecycle state selection, project isolation and developer attribution, tombstones and poisoned content.
Run against the public file/skill/lifecycle surfaces present in v0.0.1 and expand as governed operations arrive.
Canaries run offline in isolated roots and make no claims of coding-outcome improvement.
stories.validation: Run the top-level release gate and retain canary results.

stories.title: Inject durable-write interrupts and successful writes with lost responses
stories.outcome: Every shipped state-changing operation has replayable failure points and idempotent retry.
acceptance: Interrupt before/after each durable write and drop responses after commit.
Rerun the same operation without duplicates, data loss or weakened semantics.
Ship lifecycle failpoints first and extend this harness to governed bank operations in v0.0.2.
stories.validation: Enumerate failpoints against real public commands and compare final state/receipts with a clean run.

stories.title: Retain incident reproductions and observed guide examples
stories.outcome: Regressions and guide examples preserve user-visible behavior and normative rules.
acceptance: Name minimal public-interface incident tests after the symptom and connect outcome/acceptance/integration/delivery to its work item.
Capture quoted commands/results/errors/exit meanings from observed test or read-only output.
Documentation refactors map every normative rule at equal/stronger force and retain route reachability.
Representative independent reviews use only runtime-loaded instructions.
stories.validation: Audit an example captured command transcript and execute route/rule-preservation checks.

stories.title: Detect and recover interrupted multi-file bank mutations
stories.outcome: A torn bank is visibly interrupted and can be finished or rolled back.
acceptance: Create an exclusive no-replace transaction marker under the bank lock with ID/paths/base hashes/operation/phase and no secrets/deleted content.
Use per-file atomic replacements, change MEMORY.md last when needed and remove marker only after verifying every target.
Readers encountering the marker avoid mutation and route to recovery.
Keep recovery journal/backups outside repository; never claim cross-file atomicity.
Protect consolidation, correction and pruning with this v0.0.1 recovery protocol; shared Git reconciliation is a separate boundary.
stories.validation: Interrupt each write and verify visible refusal plus finish/rollback convergence.

stories.title: Verify a clean bank is complete without generated state
stories.outcome: A fresh agent can resume solely from current routed Markdown.
acceptance: All visible scope/current/stale status is understandable.
No active transaction marker is present.
No index/database/MCP/hook/federation/cache/recovery journal is required for usability.
stories.validation: Delete all generated state in a clean fixture and perform bounded resume; reject interrupted fixtures.

stories.title: Preview, apply and verify identity binding before scoped operations
stories.outcome: Status and scope/bind expose one identity algorithm shared by all clients.
acceptance: Show resolved IDs and supporting evidence in status.
Resolve developer attribution and project identity before mediated writes or federation export; reject ambiguity.
Scope/bind previews bank/registry changes, preserves aliases and reads back the result.
Adapters cannot invent alternate project-ID algorithms.
stories.validation: Invoke status/bind against unambiguous and conflicting fixtures and verify registry/bank readback.

stories.title: Initialize from existing memory, code, ADRs and AWA work evidence
stories.outcome: Initialization builds a useful orientation map and surfaces unresolved product conflicts.
acceptance: Inventory and preserve existing memory before creation; inspect docs, code/tests, ADRs and AWA projects/tasks/release milestones.
Link to authorities and record useful missing context without duplicating source documents or inventing requirements.
Distinguish intent, implementation and planned work; genuine internal contradictions trigger focused PM Q&A with the detecting developer.
AWA unavailability reports an evidence gap while local inspection remains available.
stories.validation: Run empty/existing bank initialization with agreeing and conflicting docs/code/ADR/AWA fixtures; verify preserved content and focused clarification.

stories.title: Keep shared memory tracked and separate from runtime and work state
stories.outcome: A configured Git bank boundary preserves the separate roles of memory, AWA and Vox.
acceptance: Track admitted project Markdown under the configured bank root and default authority branch.
Exclude raw transcripts, credentials and runtime/cache/recovery artifacts; provide no personal memory layer.
Keep local use independent of AWA/Vox availability and avoid a duplicate tracker or message bus.
stories.validation: Validate included/excluded Git paths and authority behavior in isolated fixtures.

stories.title: Represent supersession, revocation and deletion safely
stories.outcome: Current guidance excludes revoked, superseded and deleted content without unsafe residual copies.
acceptance: Keep only safe explanations for inactive guidance.
Use durable content-free tombstones when any projection could recreate deleted data.
Rebuild and consolidation cannot resurrect deleted content or reversible/low-entropy content hashes.
stories.validation: Run selective-forgetting and tombstone-content canaries.

stories.title: Enforce observed writes and disposable projections
stories.outcome: Mediated writes detect conflicts and every projection is bound to source revisions.
acceptance: Hold the ADR-0010 lock from inventory through readback; replace files atomically after observed-content checks.
Multi-file operations use recovery markers and do not claim global atomicity.
Optional event writers use idempotency keys and projections record source revisions/digests.
Any optional SQLite store remains disposable and cannot hold the sole admitted record.
stories.validation: Run conflicting-write, idempotency and projection-source-binding contract tests.

stories.title: Validate the route graph and normative guide contract
stories.outcome: Publishing and activation reject mechanically invalid or unreachable skill packs.
acceptance: Check exactly one SKILL.md, frontmatter, all relative file/anchor links, reachability and unconditional-load cycles.
Validate required leaf sections/order/backlinks, executable modes, referenced schemas/templates and command-to-dispatch or file-operation mapping.
Check mechanical RFC 2119 forms without claiming keyword count establishes semantic completeness.
Documentation refactors retain a rule/strength/location map and representative independent usage review.
stories.validation: Run positive pack validation and deliberately malformed route, link, frontmatter and leaf fixtures.

stories.title: Expose the deterministic CLI and honest file-only fallback
stories.outcome: A client-neutral command surface validates the bank while raw Markdown remains usable.
acceptance: One portable skill plus deterministic CLI implements the same contract for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and custom harnesses.
Expose public CLI operation groups with project identity, developer attribution, memory IDs, applicability, validity and provenance as relevant.
Support automatic durable learning and memory-only Git exchange at turn boundaries without requiring MCP, hooks, a plugin or a daemon.
Preserve a readable file-only/manual fallback without claiming mediated guarantees.
Preserve unrelated client configuration and use short activation bindings, never a separate client policy or identity algorithm.
stories.validation: Invoke the installed CLI and demonstrate fresh-agent resume with it removed.

stories.title: Filter before ranking and explain baseline retrieval
stories.outcome: Scope-safe recall works through routes, identifiers and ordinary text search.
acceptance: Apply project authorization, active validity/time, trust/type and contextual applicability filters before ranking.
Explain every selected memory and use exact IDs/paths and text search as the baseline.
Optional semantic, temporal or graph ranking can be removed without losing baseline recall.
stories.validation: Run scope, stale, trust, exact-match and explanation fixtures with all optional indexes disabled.

stories.title: Enforce mediated trust, privacy and injection boundaries
stories.outcome: Mediated operations persist and retrieve only within explicit safety boundaries.
acceptance: Separate user, assistant, tool, external and verified-repository source classes.
Authorize repository/project scope before recall and require approval for cross-project/procedural promotion.
Scan/redact secrets, limit content/size, quarantine suspected instructions or unverifiable identity.
Audit mediated admission/mutation/retrieval/promotion and invalidate deleted data.
Never interpolate retrieved text into shell commands or execute commands because memory contains them.
Apply source classification, secret scanning, scope, quarantine and reviewed-procedure boundaries before automatic shared-memory commits in v0.0.1.
Routine capture authorization never permits secret/raw conversation export or procedural promotion.
stories.validation: Exercise secret, poisoning, identity, oversized-input, approval and audit fixtures.

stories.title: Test true concurrent processes and observed-write conflicts
stories.outcome: Concurrent bank writers cannot silently overwrite each other.
acceptance: Use actual competing processes on the same temporary bank.
Prove lock recovery, observed-hash checks, atomic replacement, bounded retry and no last-write-wins loss.
Distinguish a worktree-local bank lock from cross-clone Git reconciliation; shared runtime locks must not enter memory commits.
stories.validation: Run synchronized process races, external-edit races and stale-lock recovery cases.

stories.title: Validate routed topics, episodes, procedure candidates and history
stories.outcome: Optional structured records remain reachable ordinary Markdown.
acceptance: Support topics/episodes/procedures/history with bounded direct or topic-index reachability.
Validate record frontmatter ID/kind/status/scope/source/validity/updated and optional trust/confidence.
Decisions link to ADRs, episodes retain bounded lessons/evidence, and procedure candidates remain non-binding until promotion.
Admitted independently useful branch discoveries can be shared with conditions; unadmitted/transient observations remain outside the bank until admitted and do not form a personal store.
Automatic consolidation preserves record identity/source links, distinct conditions and all developer/session provenance; the router stays bounded.
stories.validation: Run record-layout, missing-route, metadata and candidate-procedure fixtures.

stories.title: Checkpoint active context as one verified observed replacement
stories.outcome: The common checkpoint changes only activeContext.md.
acceptance: Capture focus, meaningful recent changes, open questions and next concrete step.
Progress, topics and router updates are separate observed writes.
Atomic replacement runs under the common lock and readback protocol.
stories.validation: Invoke checkpoint and verify all other canonical file contents remain unchanged.

stories.title: Recover Git sharing and reconcile deletions through later code merges
stories.outcome: Retries and ordinary branch integration preserve readable canonical memory.
acceptance: Keep local capture useful offline; report sharing as pending/stale and never claim unverified freshness.
Inventory current Git state on retry, recover lost successful push/merge responses and avoid duplicate publication.
Treat cursor/retry state as disposable; loss may require reconciliation but cannot lose canonical Markdown.
Reconcile deletion/tombstones/pruned guidance and later ordinary code merge/rebase without resurrection, duplication or reversal.
stories.validation: Inject failure/offline/lost-response/cursor-loss and later ordinary code merge cases against isolated remotes.

stories.title: Assemble bounded diverse context with source and status labels
stories.outcome: Retrieved context fits its budget and retains unresolved contradictions.
acceptance: Enforce token/content budgets without dropping provenance or lifecycle labels.
Include unresolved contradictory evidence and prefer diverse useful types over duplicate results.
stories.validation: Compare assembled contexts against budget, provenance, contradiction and duplication fixtures.

stories.title: Package the complete client-neutral portable artifact
stories.outcome: One self-contained skills/agent-memory artifact can operate the implemented protocol.
acceptance: Include one SKILL.md, progressive guides, scripts, schemas and templates.
Follow the linked lifecycle blueprint; mark adapters separately without core dependencies on client APIs or marketplaces.
stories.validation: Copy the artifact to an isolated location and validate every implemented route/asset.

stories.title: Find and reconcile existing learning before every write and landing
stories.outcome: Automatic capture avoids semantic duplicates and preserves distinct learning.
acceptance: Consult the router, search same-concept and alternative wording, and read plausible matches with evidence and conditions before changing memory.
Update/merge equivalent learning; keep genuinely distinct facts separate with stable identities.
Interrupted/unavailable memory does not prove absence; publication repeats the comparison against newly landed main.
No vector index is required; preserve source/provenance/conditions when combining learning.
stories.validation: Run same-concept paraphrase, near-match, distinct-condition, interrupted-bank and concurrent-duplicate scenarios.

stories.title: Admit small evidenced records and quarantine unsafe candidates
stories.outcome: Capture and durable admission remain distinct, reviewable stages.
acceptance: Admission considers utility, evidence confidence, novelty, durability, scope, type and security classification.
User statements and verified tools may follow deterministic rules; assistant inferences/external text require stronger evidence or review.
Untrusted content cannot promote procedures or global preferences automatically.
Automatically capture durable discoveries, verified fixes, useful failed approaches, user corrections and confirmed decisions without per-record approval.
Assistant proposals and unanswered suggestions remain unconfirmed; label uncertainty and do not accumulate raw transcripts, redundant source facts, or copied work state.
stories.validation: Run admission/quarantine fixtures across source classes and attempted instruction promotion.

stories.title: Expose lifecycle commands and separate runtime, state and data
stories.outcome: A managed installation has one shared artifact and an external ownership receipt.
acceptance: Provide install, uninstall, update --check, update, version, doctor and status.
Use XDG-compatible managed source; keep memory data, runtime state, caches and indexes in distinct paths.
Store receipt and recoverable backups outside the checkout at the specified XDG state location.
Support generic, Codex, Claude, OpenCode, custom and no-client-link targets.
stories.validation: Run installed command discovery in temporary homes and inspect the receipt/target layout.

stories.title: Consolidate idempotently with source links and events
stories.outcome: Maintenance proposes deduplication and higher-order patterns without destructive history rewrites.
acceptance: Run outside the foreground task by default without requiring a background daemon.
Preserve evidence and derivation links, emit events and converge on repeat execution.
Procedure promotion remains a separate reviewed operation.
Automatically combine duplicates and tighten wording at natural turn boundaries, preserving distinct conditions, evidence, all developer/session provenance and useful correction history.
Keep routine success quiet; promptly surface conflicts, failures and consequential corrections.
Unresolved changes of meaning route to the detecting developer; do not invent higher-order decisions.
stories.validation: Repeat consolidation on duplicates, conflicts and revoked/deleted source fixtures.

stories.title: Keep forgetting operations distinct and propagate invalidation
stories.outcome: Expiration, supersession, revocation, deletion and retention remove guidance appropriately.
acceptance: Expose separate operations with the shared lifecycle semantics.
Invalidate every materialized view/cache/index.
Deleted memory cannot reappear from cached retrieval or consolidation output.
Automatically prune incorrect or irrelevant guidance only when stronger evidence establishes it; age alone does not justify pruning.
Preserve narrower applicability for older branches/environments and a concise safe correction or supersession explanation.
Ask the detecting developer when evidence is ambiguous; explicit deletion still uses safe tombstones.
stories.validation: Run end-to-end forgetting/rebuild/reconsolidation fixtures.

stories.title: Install idempotently with preflight, ownership and verified activation
stories.outcome: Install safely activates owned targets and preserves unrelated user content.
acceptance: Inventory/plan and preflight all targets before changes, stage backups, activate atomically per target, read back and write a verified receipt.
Refuse unrelated files/directories/symlinks; link and copy modes converge on the same digest.
Preserve replaced managed copies and sentinel surroundings; install wrappers atomically.
Report revision/version/dirty qualification/digest/adapters/data location; restart guidance appears only when loaded content changes.
stories.validation: Run fresh/repeat, collision, copy/link, spaces, sentinel-edit and partial-activation rollback tests from the lifecycle blueprint.

stories.title: Guard updates and recover interrupted multi-target activation
stories.outcome: A verified fast-forward update preserves data and can resume or roll back.
acceptance: Lock lifecycle operations and bind channel to recorded remote/ref.
Refuse dirty/unexpected/downgrade/non-fast-forward candidates; update --check is read-only.
Validate candidate before activation; journal per-target switches and verify all client-visible targets/command.
Failed validation retains the prior installation; lost responses and interrupted activation converge on retry without global atomicity claims.
stories.validation: Use temporary local remotes and failpoints before/after each durable update write.

stories.title: Remove owned runtime safely and preview any explicit data purge
stories.outcome: Ordinary uninstall preserves memory, unrelated settings, user edits and backups.
acceptance: Inventory/preview owned targets against the external receipt; remove only proven unchanged ownership.
Restore sentinel-managed surroundings, preserve modified targets and keep data/projections/backups.
Retain an uninstall receipt and reinstall instructions; remove managed source only when no active target references it.
A distinct purge requires exact paths/counts and confirmation; refuse unresolved broad paths, symlink escapes, home or filesystem root.
stories.validation: Run uninstall/reinstall, modified-target, missing-source-receipt and bounded explicit purge fixtures.

stories.title: Report version, cheap status and actionable doctor recovery
stories.outcome: Users can diagnose installation identity, bank health and interrupted operations.
acceptance: Version reports source/version/revision/digest/cleanliness/mode/channel/receipt schema.
Status is cheap/read-only and reports resolved identities, store/bank state, enabled adapters and pending transactions.
Doctor checks prerequisites, permissions, ownership, routes, wrappers, links/blocks, schema compatibility and enabled optional surfaces.
Separate warnings/failures and provide bounded repairs; interrupted lifecycle operations and lost responses are resumable or safely rollbackable.
stories.validation: Invoke actual commands against healthy and intentionally broken isolated installations.

stories.title: Combine compatible learning and escalate contradictions to the detecting developer
stories.outcome: Semantic conflicts are resolved explicitly without blocking unrelated work.
acceptance: Combine same-file compatible changes and semantic duplicates, retaining distinct conditions, evidence/provenance/history.
Inspect same-subject/overlapping-condition contradictions even in separate files and textually clean Git merges.
Show both claims/evidence to the current detecting developer; identify other-developer attribution and recommend clarification as needed without automatic messaging.
Pause only disputed updates/dependent work, continue independent work, and never choose truth by last writer/identity/recency.
Record the clarifying decision and correct/supersede guidance safely.
stories.validation: Run yellow/blue, differently worded duplicate, disjoint-condition, cross-developer and independent-work fixtures.

stories.title: Gate releases with isolated real-command lifecycle tests
stories.outcome: Lifecycle safety is proven through the installed user-facing surface.
acceptance: Cover the full ADR and linked-blueprint matrix: fresh/reinstall, link/copy/custom/no-client, conflicts, update/ref guards, interrupts/lost responses, rollback/locks, uninstall/purge and preserved data.
Verify all enabled clients resolve the same revision/digest and generated-state deletion does not impair resume.
Validate the pack before publication and update activation.
Tests never use real credentials, mutate live client config/data/developer checkouts or require the network by default.
stories.validation: Run the complete temporary-home CLI lifecycle gate with deterministic failpoints.

stories.title: Automatically land memory-only changes through repository rules
stories.outcome: Admitted learning can land independently of feature code.
acceptance: Use current shared memory as publication base; preserve non-memory staged/work files and exclude feature ancestry.
Follow permissions/checks/review/branch rules; required human review stays pending, with no force push or bypass.
Repeat deduplication and semantic review before landing; reconcile a racing main head and read back actual landing.
Retain applicability/evidence for independently useful unmerged discoveries.
stories.validation: Run memory-only publication with feature-code ancestors, dirty/staged unrelated paths, competing main, required review and lost response fixtures.

stories.title: Reconcile only landed memory into each branch at turn boundaries
stories.outcome: New shared learning arrives without rebasing or importing feature code.
acceptance: Three-way compare last-observed shared, current local, and incoming shared memory; preserve unpublished local learning.
Change only allowed memory paths, preserve unrelated index/work files and branch history, and do not snapshot-overwrite memory.
Read relevant imports with provenance/conditions; do not imply branch code changed.
Support explicit harness-neutral invocation without required hooks, daemon or mid-turn interruption.
stories.validation: Refresh stale-code/dirty-memory worktrees from a second clone and verify exact non-memory and history preservation.

stories.title: Prove shared learning survives independent clones and concurrent sessions
stories.outcome: Two developers and multiple harnesses exchange correct memory without changing feature code.
acceptance: Exercise independent clones, worktrees, branches, developer identities and harness/session identities through public user-facing operations on an isolated remote.
Preserve non-memory files/index/history while publishing from unfinished work and recalling at the next successful boundary.

Cover concurrent compatible edits, duplicates before write/landing, semantic yellow/blue contradictions, stale code and conditional applicability, evidence-based pruning and contradictory initialization evidence.
Cover offline/retry/lost-success-response and later ordinary code merge without loss, duplication or resurrection; only disputed memory/dependent work pauses.
stories.validation: Run the isolated end-to-end multi-clone/worktree acceptance matrix with snapshots of unrelated Git state.

stories.title: Gate v0.0.1 on the complete quiet cross-machine learning loop
stories.outcome: The first release proves useful shared learning across developers and harnesses.
acceptance: One session publishes from unfinished feature work; another harness on another clone recalls at its next successful boundary without code changes.
Include two developers, races, compatible edits, duplicates, semantic conflicts, conditions, pruning, retry and later code merge.
Routine successful maintenance is quiet; conflicts, failures and consequential corrections surface promptly at boundaries.
No real credentials or live repositories/client data are used by acceptance tests.

Every other v0.0.1 story is Done at its reviewed-merge delivery boundary before the complete release gate can pass; include lifecycle, portable artifact, security, identity, storage and learning outcomes as well as sharing.
